findings.text: Calculations follow a similar split. Tally's calculated fields are part of the same free conditional logic system, with no separate paywall . WPForms bundles its Calculations addon into the Pro plan rather than Basic, according to its own pricing page. Jotform's formula capability is described in that same WPForms comparison as "widget only," which is worth confirming directly if a live, editable formula engine (rather than a static widget) is what your quote calculator needs.
findings.reason: Jotform's 'widget only' formula claim is misattributed to the WPForms comparison; it actually comes from Tally's own Jotform comparison page.

findings.text: Payments. Tally lists payment collection as one of its input blocks, and its conditional logic documentation states you can show or hide "any block," which by that same logic includes a payment block, letting you reveal a checkout field only for respondents who choose a paid option. WPForms ties conditional logic on payment fields specifically to its Pro tier, where the Stripe Pro, Square Pro, or PayPal Commerce integrations let the price shown, or whether a payment field appears at all, change based on earlier answers.
findings.reason: Claims conditional logic can specifically show/hide a Tally payment block based on prior answers; no source confirms this combination, only general 'any block' wording.
